items.html: Plant foods carry bacteria too. The worry about bacteria covers food from both plant and animal sources: Escherichia coli outbreaks have come from bagged spinach and romaine lettuce, and Salmonella recalls have included watermelon, onions, cantaloupe and cucumbers, so avoiding animal foods does not remove the risk.
cites: PAJ5200.FoodSafety-micro.pptx, Slide 9, 15, 16, 18, 31 and 32

src.question: A household eats no meat, eggs or dairy. Does that remove its risk of bacterial foodborne illness?
src.key: No; plant foods carry bacteria too
src.explanation: The worry about bacteria covers food from both plant and animal sources. Escherichia coli outbreaks have come from bagged spinach and romaine lettuce, and Salmonella recalls have included watermelon, onions, cantaloupe and cucumbers, so avoiding animal foods does not remove the risk.

items.html: Recorded counts are probably too low. The yearly estimate of foodborne illness is probably an under-reported number, and Campylobacter jejuni illness in particular is very much under-reported, so recorded counts likely understate the true burden.
cites: PAJ5200.FoodSafety-micro.pptx, Slide 9, 21 and 34

src.question: How do recorded counts of foodborne illness compare with the true number of cases?
src.explanation: The yearly estimate of foodborne illness is described as probably an under-reported number, and Campylobacter jejuni illness in particular is very much under-reported. Many people who fall ill are never counted, so recorded counts likely understate the true burden.

items.html: Typhoid fever, caused by Salmonella typhi, is the most severe enteric fever, marked by invasion of the intestinal (gut) wall, with possible spread to the blood and lymph nodes.
cites: PAJ5200.FoodSafety-micro.pptx, Slide 17, 23, 27 and 33

src.question: Which feature describes typhoid fever, the most severe enteric fever?
src.key: Invasion of the gut wall, then blood and nodes
src.explanation: Typhoid fever, caused by Salmonella typhi, is the most severe enteric fever, and it is marked by invasion of the intestinal wall, with possible spread to the blood and lymph nodes. Other forms of salmonellosis include gastroenteritis, septicemia, fever, shock and kidney dysfunction.

items.html: Mary Mallon, “Typhoid Mary.” She was warned and given an explanation, yet she kept cooking despite warnings: she persisted in preparing food, causing multiple deadly outbreaks.
cites: PAJ5200.FoodSafety-micro.pptx, Slide 17, 18 and 20 and image on Slide 20

src.question: Why is Mary Mallon, known as Typhoid Mary, remembered in food safety?
src.key: She kept cooking despite warnings, causing outbreaks
src.explanation: Mary Mallon was warned and given an explanation, yet she persisted in preparing food and caused multiple deadly outbreaks. Typhoid fever, caused by Salmonella typhi, is the most severe enteric fever, so a single person handling food could spread it widely.

items.html: Acquiring Blastomyces dermatitidis. People acquire it by inhaling its conidia when the soil is disturbed; the inhaled conidia convert to yeasts and multiply in the lungs, causing cough, chest pain and fever.
cites: PAJ5200.Fungi of Medical importance.pptx, Slide 12, 24, 33, 52 and 65

src.question: Blastomyces dermatitidis lives in forest soil, decaying wood and animal manure. How do people usually acquire it?
src.explanation: People inhale the conidia when the soil is disturbed; the inhaled conidia (10 to 100) convert to yeasts and multiply in the lungs, causing cough, chest pain and fever. Chronic skin nodules and later bone and nervous system complications can follow.

items.html: An emerging concern. Mycoses account for a growing share of nosocomial (hospital-acquired) infections, about one in ten and rising, which is why opportunistic fungi are an emerging concern.
cites: PAJ5200.Fungi of Medical importance.pptx, Slide 4, 7 and 19

src.question: Why are opportunistic mycoses described as an emerging medical concern?
src.key: Their share of nosocomial infections is rising
src.explanation: Mycoses account for a growing share of nosocomial (hospital-acquired) infections, about one in ten and rising, which is why opportunistic fungi are an emerging concern. They need impaired host defenses (human immunodeficiency virus infection, cancer, diabetes, autoimmune disorders) and cause illness from superficial colonization to fatal systemic disease.

items.html: Treating systemic cryptococcal infection. It generally requires amphotericin B plus fluconazole or another azole-type drug; treatment protocols are well established for patients with human immunodeficiency virus infection.
cites: PAJ5200.Fungi of Medical importance.pptx, Slide 39, 45, 56, 57 and 58

src.question: Which regimen does systemic cryptococcal infection generally require?
src.explanation: Systemic cryptococcal infection generally requires amphotericin B and fluconazole or another azole-type drug. Treatment protocols are well established for patients with human immunodeficiency virus infection, though the drugs may be unavailable in many countries.

items.html: Acquiring Aspergillus. Aspergillus is a very common airborne soil fungus: people usually acquire it by breathing in airborne spores, and infection usually occurs in the lungs, where its spores germinate and form fungal balls.
cites: PAJ5200.Fungi of Medical importance.pptx, Slide 39, 45, 52 and 60

src.question: How do people usually acquire Aspergillus infection of the lungs?
src.explanation: Aspergillus is a very common airborne soil fungus, and infection usually occurs in the lungs, where its spores germinate and form fungal balls. People at serious risk include those with human immunodeficiency virus infection, leukemia or a transplant.

items.html: Not caught from another person. Histoplasmosis is not transmitted person to person, so a spouse cannot catch it from him; people acquire it by inhaling conidia from moist soil enriched with bird or bat guano.
cites: PAJ5200.Fungi of Medical importance.pptx, Slide 12 and 26 and image on Slide 28

src.question: A man is hospitalized with disseminated histoplasmosis, and his wife asks whether she could catch it from him. What is accurate?
src.key: She cannot catch it from him
src.explanation: Histoplasmosis is not transmitted person to person. People acquire it by inhaling conidia from moist soil enriched with bird or bat guano, and in the body the fungus lives as a yeast inside phagocytes, not as an infective spore.

items.html: Paracoccidioidomycosis risk profile. Rural farm workers and harvesters are most at risk; poor nutrition (a poorly nourished worker) is a predisposing factor, and male sex and age over 40 add to the risk.
cites: PAJ5200.Fungi of Medical importance.pptx, Slide 30, 37, 39 and 64

src.question: Which person fits the risk profile for paracoccidioidomycosis?
src.key: Poorly nourished male farm worker over 40
src.explanation: In the cool, humid soils of Central and South America, rural farm workers and harvesters are most at risk; poor nutrition is a predisposing factor, and male sex and age over 40 add to the risk. All of those clues are present here.

items.html: Diagnosing cryptococcosis. Biochemical and serological tests are the best diagnostic tools; a negative stain can demonstrate the encapsulated budding yeast.
cites: PAJ5200.Fungi of Medical importance.pptx, Slide 33, 56 and 57 and image on Slide 17

src.question: Which methods are the best tools for diagnosing cryptococcosis?
src.explanation: For cryptococcosis, biochemical and serological testing are the best diagnostic tools. A negative stain can demonstrate the encapsulated budding yeast, and systemic infection generally requires amphotericin B with fluconazole or another azole.

items.html: Candida auris outbreaks. Hospital outbreaks are hard to eradicate because of drug, heat and disinfectant resistance: it shows antifungal drug resistance, is thermoresistant and is partially resistant to common disinfectants.
cites: PAJ5200.Fungi of Medical importance.pptx, Slide 5, 14, 30, 52, 56 and 57

src.question: Which traits make hospital outbreaks of Candida auris hard to eradicate?
src.explanation: Candida auris is emerging as a serious cause of invasive candidiasis, with hospital outbreaks that are difficult to eradicate: it shows antifungal drug resistance, is thermoresistant and is partially resistant to common disinfectants. It was first identified in an ear infection, hence its name.

items.html: Saprobic. A saprobe feeds on dead or decaying matter, deriving its nutrition from it; Sporothrix schenckii is a very common saprobic fungus that decomposes plant matter in soil.
cites: PAJ5200.Fungi of Medical importance.pptx, Slide 5, 12, 39 and 53

src.question: Sporothrix schenckii is a saprobic fungus. What does saprobic mean?
src.key: It feeds on dead or decaying matter
src.explanation: A saprobe derives its nutrition from dead or decaying matter. Sporothrix schenckii is a very common saprobic fungus that decomposes plant matter in soil, which is why thorns, wood, bare roots, pine straw and hay carry it to people.

items.html: Keeping down dust. Coccidioides arthrospores are inhaled from dust, so prevention targets dust: oiling roads to keep down dust, planting to minimize erosion and using dust masks.
cites: PAJ5200.Fungi of Medical importance.pptx, Slide 12, 19, 26, 30 and 56

src.question: Which community measure reduces inhalation of Coccidioides spores in an endemic area?
src.key: Oiling roads to keep down dust
src.explanation: Coccidioides arthrospores are inhaled from dust, so prevention targets dust: oiling roads, planting to minimize erosion and using dust masks. Farming, road construction or repair, archaeological digs, landslides and dust storms all raise exposure.

items.html: Fusarium and the eye. Fusarium species, a mainly tropical soil mold, occasionally infect the eyes, for example through contaminated contact lenses, as well as toenails, feet and burned skin.
cites: PAJ5200.Fungi of Medical importance.pptx, Slide 12, 63, 64 and 65

src.question: How can Fusarium reach and infect the eye?
src.explanation: Fusarium species, a mainly tropical soil mold, occasionally infect the eyes, for example through contaminated contact lenses, as well as toenails, feet and burned skin, and can result in severe disability and death.

items.html: The rarest primary mycosis. Paracoccidioidomycosis is the rarest of the primary mycoses; systemic disease is not common, and infections are usually mild and self-limiting.
cites: PAJ5200.Fungi of Medical importance.pptx, Slide 5, 7, 26 and 37 and image on Slide 13

src.question: Which description fits paracoccidioidomycosis?
src.explanation: Paracoccidioidomycosis, endemic in Central and South America (mainly the cool, humid soils of Brazil, Colombia, Venezuela, Argentina and Paraguay), is the rarest of the primary mycoses; systemic disease is not common, and infections are usually mild and self-limiting.

items.html: True (primary) fungal pathogen. Its defining ability is invading and growing in a healthy host; an opportunist, by contrast, has little or no virulence of its own and needs impaired host defenses.
cites: PAJ5200.Fungi of Medical importance.pptx, Slide 5, 7 and 12

src.question: Which ability defines a true (primary) fungal pathogen?
src.key: Invading and growing in a healthy host
src.explanation: A true or primary fungal pathogen can invade and grow in a healthy host. Its most striking adaptation is the switch from hyphal cells to yeast cells with the change to host temperature. An opportunist, by contrast, has little or no virulence of its own and needs impaired host defenses.

items.html: Opportunistic mycosis. A fungus with few, if any, virulence factors that infects a host weakened by corticosteroids is an opportunistic mycosis: these fungi usually start infection in immunocompromised hosts.
cites: PAJ5200.Fungi of Medical importance.pptx, Slide 5, 7, 14, 22 and 42

src.question: A fungus with few, if any, virulence factors causes a systemic infection in a patient taking long-term corticosteroids. How is this mycosis best classified?
src.explanation: Few, if any, virulence factors plus a host weakened by corticosteroids is the picture of an opportunistic mycosis: these fungi usually start infection in immunocompromised hosts, and predisposing factors such as primary illness, corticosteroid use, diabetes and cancer should be considered.

items.html: Number one cause of food-related deaths. Listeria monocytogenes is the number one cause of food-related deaths in the United States.
cites: PAJ5200.FoodSafety-micro.pptx, Slide 23, 21, 17 and 28

src.question: Which ranking does Listeria monocytogenes hold among foodborne agents in the United States?
src.key: Number one cause of food-related deaths
src.explanation: Listeria monocytogenes is the number one cause of food-related deaths in the United States. The groups at greatest risk for listeriosis are pregnant women, unborn children, premature babies, elderly people and immunocompromised people.

items.html: Poultry, including its leftovers. Even one drop of raw poultry fluid can cause Campylobacter jejuni illness, so holiday poultry and its leftovers deserve particular care.
cites: PAJ5200.FoodSafety-micro.pptx, Slide 18, 21, 28 and 32 and image on Slide 21

src.question: Which food calls for particular care to prevent Campylobacter jejuni illness?
src.explanation: Campylobacter jejuni comes with poultry: even one drop of raw poultry fluid can cause illness, and holiday poultry and its leftovers deserve particular care. In its transmission cycle, chickens and poultry meat lead to people.

items.html: Live backyard hens. Keeping live poultry such as backyard hens is a Salmonella source, alongside poultry products, eggs and pet food.
cites: PAJ5200.FoodSafety-micro.pptx, Slide 17, 18, 23, 25 and 31

src.question: Which household exposure is a known source of Salmonella?
src.explanation: Live poultry such as backyard hens is a Salmonella source alongside poultry products, eggs and pet food, which fits its association mainly with poultry and aquatic reptiles. Raw honey and garden soil, by contrast, are where clostridial spores are found.

items.html: Not every strain is pathogenic. Escherichia coli is found everywhere, including inside humans, but it is not always pathogenic and has many good traits too; illness comes from the bad strains.
cites: PAJ5200.FoodSafety-micro.pptx, Slide 15, 17, 25 and 31

src.question: Escherichia coli is found everywhere, including inside healthy humans. What explains its presence without disease?
src.explanation: Escherichia coli is found everywhere, including inside humans, but it is not always pathogenic and has many good traits too. Illness comes from the bad strains, which can carry numerous toxins (for example enterotoxigenic or enterohemorrhagic strains).

items.html: Law enforcement and policy. Local and state health departments, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, the Food and Drug Administration and the United States Department of Agriculture all conduct surveillance and investigate outbreaks, but enforcing food safety law and policy rests with the Food and Drug Administration and the United States Department of Agriculture.
cites: PAJ5200.FoodSafety-micro.pptx, Slide 9, 34 and 35

src.question: Which food safety responsibility rests with the Food and Drug Administration and the United States Department of Agriculture rather than with local and state health departments?
src.key: Enforcing food safety law and policy
src.explanation: Local and state health departments, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, the Food and Drug Administration and the United States Department of Agriculture all conduct surveillance and investigate outbreaks, but the Food and Drug Administration and the United States Department of Agriculture are in charge of law enforcement and policy enactment.

items.html: Why norovirus spreads so readily. A few viral particles can infect: its infectious dose is only a few viral particles, and it spreads person to person through feces and vomitus in daycares, nursing homes and cruise ships.
cites: PAJ5200.FoodSafety-micro.pptx, Slide 33, 23, 25 and 12

src.question: Why does norovirus spread so readily in daycares and nursing homes?
src.key: A few viral particles can infect
src.explanation: The infectious dose of norovirus is only a few viral particles, and it spreads person to person through feces and vomitus. Together these drive outbreaks in daycares, nursing homes and cruise ships.

items.html: Protozoan diarrhea sources. Protozoans such as Cryptosporidium, Cyclospora, Giardia and Entamoeba cause mild diarrhea associated with uncooked produce (fruits and vegetables) and drinking water.
cites: PAJ5200.FoodSafety-micro.pptx, Slide 32, 29 and 25

src.question: Foodborne protozoan diarrhea is associated with which sources?
src.explanation: Protozoans such as Cryptosporidium, Cyclospora, Giardia and Entamoeba cause mild diarrhea associated with uncooked fruits and vegetables or drinking water. Ready-to-eat salad bags are a common culprit of foodborne illness.
